blocks.x: A working build of Data & Lakehouse inside Public Sector & Government: the operating context that shapes it, the services sequenced through the method, and the deltas we commit to.

In Public Sector & Government, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Benefits, tax, health and licensing systems never joined; citizens re-submit the same facts to every agency. Fraud and error hide in the seams.
Permits, claims and case files are paper-shaped; processing times measured in months erode trust and increase cost per case.
Aging systems with hardening debt meet rising state-grade threats; accreditation cycles slow every change.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Under the hood the pattern composes 7 Data, Analytics & Lakehouse services — Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics as the usual core — sequenced by the Dataq Method, with EU AI Act obligations shaping design decisions from the first sprint onward.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
Event-driven, consent-aware data sharing between agencies with lineage (tell-us-once services enabled)
Service metrics aligned to delivery cadence with certified definitions (delivery decisions on real numbers)
First-contact resolution up sharply with grounded assistants

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EU AI Act and Security accreditation (FedRAMP-class / national schemes). Cloud and system authorization duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
